name: IEC postponed output qualifier
summary: Angle mark beside an output showing it changes only when the initiating input returns to its original level.
description: The postponed output qualifier is a small right-angle mark inside the outline next to an output. It indicates that the output changes when the input that initiated the change, typically the C input, returns to its initial external state. It identifies pulse-triggered or master-slave flip-flops and data lock-out types.

This matters for timing analysis. On a pulse-triggered device the data must be stable for the whole time the clock is active, whereas on an edge-triggered device only setup and hold around the edge matter. The mark tells the reader which rule applies.
The qualifier does not distinguish a pulse-triggered element from a data lock-out element; the clock input marking does. A dynamic mark on C with a postponed output indicates the data lock-out form.
readingNotes: Find the mark at each Q output of a flip-flop.
Check the C input for a dynamic mark to identify the data lock-out type.
drawingChecklist: Draw the mark inside the outline at the output.
Note data stability requirements for pulse-triggered devices.
distinction: An edge-triggered flip-flop has a dynamic C input and no postponed output mark.
